ERCOT public market and operations reports
Public Utility Commission of Texas materials
Texas legislative and public reporting on Winter Storm Uri

_meta.note: Exploratory 12-phase N-D-C baseline for real-time grid cascade failure. Values are structured estimates for model demonstration and should be replaced with audited event time-series data where available.

synthetic.label: AI structured baseline
synthetic.description: Generated from public ERCOT Uri materials for phase-map demonstration.

0.name: Weather forecast and demand expectation
0.transformation: Cold-weather demand scenario enters system operations planning

1.name: Natural gas production and fuel supply
1.transformation: Gas and fuel availability prepared for power generation

2.name: Fuel transport and gas-electric dependency
2.transformation: Fuel delivered to generators through dependent pipeline and power systems

3.name: Generation winterization and plant readiness
3.transformation: Generation assets prepared to operate in extreme cold

4.name: Generation dispatch and fleet availability
4.transformation: Available MW dispatched into ERCOT market and grid operations

5.name: Transmission network and interconnection limits
5.transformation: Bulk power moved across ERCOT with limited external transfer support

6.name: Control room frequency balancing
6.transformation: Supply and demand balanced in real time to preserve frequency

7.name: Load shedding and emergency operations
7.transformation: Involuntary load reductions applied to avoid total system collapse

8.name: Distribution feeder outage management
8.transformation: Distribution utilities implement feeder-level outages and restoration sequencing

9.name: Critical services and dependent infrastructure
9.transformation: Electricity availability affects water, heat, hospitals, telecom, and public safety

10.name: Customer outage exposure and public communication
10.transformation: Households and businesses experience outage duration, communication, and access limits

11.name: Emergency restoration and black-start readiness
11.transformation: Generation, transmission, distribution, and customer service restored after crisis

0.notes: Forecasting and public warning were visible, but forecast awareness did not translate into adequate physical readiness across fuel and generation systems.

extreme_weather_forecast_flag.note: Cold-weather risk was visible before peak system failure.

1.notes: Fuel production and supply were not reliably available when thermal generators needed them. This is an upstream physical dependency failure.

fuel_supply_failure.note: Natural gas supply disruption was a documented failure channel.

2.notes: Gas-electric dependency became recursive: power was needed to move fuel, while fuel was needed to generate power.

gas_electric_dependency_failure.note: Coupled gas and electric infrastructure failure documented.

3.notes: Winterization was the deepest preventive lifecycle failure. Plant readiness did not meet the physical requirement of extreme cold operation.

winterization_failure.note: Generator weatherization failures were publicly documented.

4.notes: Generation fleet availability collapsed under cold-weather stress. The physical output, available MW, fell far below required demand.

generation_outage_failure.note: Large-scale generator outages documented during Uri.

5.notes: Transmission and interconnection limits constrained external support. ERCOT islanding increased dependence on internal capacity.

external_interconnection_limit.note: Limited external transfer capability during crisis.

6.notes: Grid control became emergency balancing. Frequency stability required involuntary load shedding to avoid full system collapse.

emergency_load_shed_flag.note: Emergency load shedding was required to preserve frequency.

7.notes: Load shedding protected the grid N-state but degraded service N-state for customers and critical infrastructure.

load_shed_failure.note: Emergency load shed became prolonged customer outage.

8.notes: Distribution-level shedding became prolonged outage. Operational contribution could not prioritize all critical load cleanly.

9.notes: End-use load included homes, hospitals, water systems, and heating demand. Downstream critical services failed when electricity delivery failed.

critical_service_cascade.note: Power outage cascaded into water, heating, and public safety impacts.

10.notes: Customer outage exposure became a public-health and household-safety failure because electricity is the support system for heat, water, communication, and medical equipment.

customer_outage_exposure.note: Needs normalized outage exposure time series.

11.notes: Emergency restoration was prolonged because generation, fuel, transmission, and distribution all needed recovery. Restoration did not behave as a simple single-phase repair.

restoration_duration.note: Needs normalized outage restoration time series.

system.interpretation: ERCOT Uri is a real-time cascade failure. Forecasting was visible, but fuel dependency, winterization, generation availability, balancing, load shedding, distribution, critical services, and customer outage exposure degraded together under cold-weather stress.
